text:
User: we need chirp ios to have search capability -- with full full-text search as provided by NMP as well as navvigating to any nevent, npub or NIP-AD -- file this as a gh issue on the chirp codebase and get a sonnet agent to start building it in a git worktree -- this should be a search button on the top-right toolbar -- launch an opus agent to decide the optimal UX we should aim for.

All the NMP primitives to make this work should be already available -- so if this is not trivial file as NMP bug because all this is supposed to already be easily possible.

Assistant: Search feature is filed and both agents are launched, in parallel with the ongoing validation sweep:

**Filed [chirp#71](https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/issues/71)** — top-right toolbar search button doing full-text NIP-50 search *and* entity navigation (nevent→thread, npub→profile, NIP-AD→resolve).

**Two agents running:**
- **Opus** → designing the optimal search UX (entry pattern, entity-vs-freetext disambiguation, result rows, resolve/loading/error states, accessibility) as a buildable spec comment on the issue.
- **Sonnet** → building it in an isolated worktree, and critically **auditing primitive exposability first**: the NMP Rust primitives (`open_search`/NIP-50, ref resolution, `nmp-nip-ad`) all exist, but `open_search` isn't yet exposed to the Swift facade (that's exactly why chirp#27 removed search). So its first job is to find the sanctioned binding path — and per your instruction, **if any of the three isn't cleanly exposable to Swift, it files an NMP bug rather than hacking around it**, since this is supposed to be trivially possible. It builds what's exposable, files for what isn't, validates each path on the sim with screenshots.

I grounded the issue and both briefs in the actual code so the "primitives already exist" claim is verified, not assumed — the real question the Sonnet agent will answer is whether the *Swift exposure* of search is trivial (Chirp facade work) or a genuine NMP binding gap.
